analysis.headline: Federal and Baja California forces arrest El Isra, a Los Rusos operator for the Mayiza, in Mexicali
analysis.what_happened: Federal and Baja California forces detained alias El Isra in a Mexicali restaurant. Local outlets describe him as a regional operator of Los Rusos, the armed wing of the Mayiza faction. Outlets give his name as Israel Leonardo or Israel Leonel Trigueros.
analysis.says_vs_does: Officials call him a priority target. The record shows one arrest; sources do not report charges, seizures or any effect on Los Rusos operations.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The arrest removes a Mayiza operator in Baja California while the Sinaloa civil war continues. Authorities gain a visible result against the Mayiza side.
tensions: Mayiza vs Chapitos: the arrest hits the Mayiza's armed wing in a border state where both factions compete.

analysis.headline: Santelices businessmen tied by the US to the Mayiza lose first court round against UIF account freeze
analysis.what_happened: Infobae reports that the Santelices businessmen lost an initial legal challenge to the UIF freeze on their accounts. OFAC had linked their security, real-estate and entertainment firms to laundering for René Arzate García, alias La Rana.
analysis.says_vs_does: The US Treasury says the network laundered money for the Mayiza's Tijuana plaza boss. The businessmen contest the freeze in court; the Mexican financial intelligence unit has kept it in place so far.
analysis.follow_the_money: Flow: alleged laundering through security, real-estate and entertainment firms for La Rana. Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The businessmen seek access to their accounts. Mexico's UIF shows that a US designation now produces a domestic freeze that holds in court.
tensions: US Treasury vs designated Mexican firms: a US listing is being tested in Mexican courts.

analysis.headline: US prosecutors charge 13 people with moving stolen and armoured US vehicles to Mexican cartels
analysis.what_happened: US authorities charged 13 people, including nine US citizens and two Mexicans, over vehicles stolen across the United States and moved from Texas into Mexico. Authorities recovered 29 vehicles, some with improvised armour.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities say the vehicles went to cartels. Milenio reports armoured trucks seized in Sonora and Sinaloa, but sources do not tie specific vehicles to a named group.
analysis.follow_the_money: The 29 recovered vehicles were valued at more than 1 million dollars. Sources do not name the buyers or payments.
analysis.at_stake: Cartels gain mobility and armour from US supply, mirroring the southbound firearms flow. US prosecutors gain a case against the southbound supply chain.
tensions: US enforcement vs southbound supply: the case targets goods flowing into Mexico rather than drugs flowing north.

analysis.headline: Marina operation captures El Primo, Los Cromos plaza boss in Oaxaca, with five more detained
analysis.what_happened: Authorities captured alias El Primo, plaza boss of Los Cromos in Ixtaltepec, Oaxaca, in an operation using a Black Hawk helicopter. Milenio reports five detained after nine Marina raids, including a Colombian national.
analysis.says_vs_does: Infobae describes Los Cromos as a CJNG-linked cell, while Milenio reports investigators probing ties to the Sinaloa Cartel. The record does not settle the cell's allegiance.
analysis.follow_the_money: Authorities had offered a reward of up to 2 million pesos. Los Cromos is accused of extortion and piso charges; sources do not give revenue figures.
analysis.at_stake: The capture targets an extortion economy on the Isthmus of Tehuantepec. Local cells gain room when larger cartels split or lose leaders.
tensions: CJNG vs Sinaloa: outlets disagree on which network Los Cromos serves.

analysis.headline: Truckers resume highway protests over robbery and extortion on Mexican roads
analysis.what_happened: El País reports that freight carriers resumed protests that again paralysed highways, citing assaults and extortion. The dispute with the government comes amid a driver shortage and financial pressure.
analysis.says_vs_does: Carriers say road security has not improved. Sources do not report new government measures in response.
analysis.follow_the_money: Extortion and cargo theft drain carrier revenue. Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Carriers use blockades as leverage for protection. The government faces disruption to freight while criminal groups keep taxing the roads.
tensions: Carriers vs federal government: blockades press for security that the state has not delivered.

analysis.headline: Over 300 US troops arrive at Colombia's Tolemaida base for counter-narcotics training
analysis.what_happened: More than 300 US military personnel arrived at the Tolemaida base in Nilo, Cundinamarca, for counter-narcotics training running from 27 October to 11 November. Separately, Colombia extradited Mocho Olmedo to the United States.
analysis.says_vs_does: The deployment is presented as training. The extradition shows Bogotá handing a suspect to Washington despite a pause in peace talks.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Washington deepens its military footprint in Colombia's drug war. Bogotá keeps security cooperation alive while Nariño violence rises.
tensions: Armed groups vs state in Nariño: the Defensoría warns of escalation after talks ended.

analysis.headline: Peru and Chile police and courts act against Tren de Aragua cells extorting transport firms
analysis.what_happened: Peruvian police captured six Venezuelans in Ate suspected of belonging to Los Gallegos, a Tren de Aragua faction extorting Lima transport firms. One had been deported and returned. A court in Iquique, Chile, upheld sentences against a Tren de Aragua cell.
analysis.says_vs_does: Deportation did not stop one suspect from returning to extort the same sector, according to Infobae.
analysis.follow_the_money: The faction extorts public-transport companies in Lima Este. Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Transport firms pay or face violence. Peru and Chile show results through arrests and convictions.
tensions: Tren de Aragua vs Andean states: deportation and arrest have not ended the extortion model.

arc_updates.text: Federal and state forces arrested El Isra, a Los Rusos operator for the Mayiza, in Mexicali.
The Santelices businessmen, linked by OFAC to the Mayiza, lost a first court challenge to the UIF account freeze.
More than 300 US troops began counter-narcotics training at Tolemaida, and Colombia extradited Mocho Olmedo to the US.
